extracted.intended_audience: IP policymakers, patent office staff, patent statisticians, researchers and analysts of patent data
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and interpreting the set of patent-related metrics, definitions and data-quality notes used in WIPO's World Intellectual Property Indicators 2023 statistical report. Covers metrics on applications, grants, patents in force, examiners, pendency, PPH, utility models, microorganism deposits, and associated methodological notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of technology (IPC concordance mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO’s International Patent Classification (IPC) technology concordance table was used to convert IPC symbols into 35 corresponding fields of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Data refer to published PCT applications. For an electronic version of the IPC technology concordance table, visit www.wipo.int/ipstats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent applications per USD 100 billion GDP
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident patent applications per USD 100 billion GDP for the top 20 origins (2012 and 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: GDP data are in 2017 US purchasing power parity (PPP) dollars. The top 20 origins were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 25 billion PPP and more than 100 resident patent applications. Because of space constraints, only the top 20 origins to fulfil these criteria are presented. Sources: WIPO Statistics Database and World Bank, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent applications per million population
rubrics_metrics.description: Resident patent applications per million population for the top 20 origins (2012 and 2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: The top 20 origins were included if they had a population greater than 5 million and if they had more than 100 resident patent applications. Because of space constraints, only the top 20 origins to fulfil these criteria are presented. Sources: WIPO Statistics Database and World Bank, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent applications per capita vs GDP per capita
rubrics_metrics.description: Scatter of resident patent applications per capita against GDP per capita (PPP constant 2017 USD), 2018–2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GDP per capita plotted on log scale. Sources: WIPO Statistics Database and World Bank, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident patent applications per capita vs R&D per capita
rubrics_metrics.description: Scatter of resident patent applications per capita against R&D expenditure per capita (R&D as percentage of GDP plotted on a log scale), 2018–2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: R&D data refer to gross domestic expenditure on research and experimental development (GERD). R&D data lag by one year. Sources: WIPO Statistics Database, OECD, UNESCO and World Bank, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents in force (trend)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trend in patents in force worldwide, 2008–2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 137 offices. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents in force by office (resident vs non-resident, non-resident share)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents in force at the top 20 offices in 2022, shown as resident and non-resident totals and non-resident share (%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: .. indicates data not available. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow of patents in force between origins and offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Flow matrix showing origin-of-patent-holder to office-of-record (selected origins and offices) for patents in force, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents in force as percentage of total applications (survival by filing year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of applications filed in year t that were in force in 2022, by application year (distribution of patents in force in 2022 as a percentage of total applications in the year of filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Percentages are calculated as the number of patent applications filed in year t and in force in 2022, divided by the total number of patent applications filed in year t. Patent holders must pay maintenance fees; they may let patents lapse before full term. Not all offices provide these data. Data for 87 offices show that 39.3% of the applications for which patents were eventually granted remained in force for at least 9 years after the application date, and about 17.8% lasted the full 20-year term. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average age of patents in force
rubrics_metrics.description: Average age of patents in force at selected offices (years), e.g., 2017 and 2022 comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: The average age of patents in force is calculated using the following formula: Σ(p*y)/Σp, where p is the number of patents in force and y the number of years between filing and reporting year. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution of patent examination outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Share of examined applications with outcomes: Granted, Rejected, Withdrawn/abandoned for selected offices (2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: The share of applications granted should not be interpreted as grant rates, as they are based on the examination date rather than the date when the application was filed. The number of grants in a given year relates to applications filed in previous years. WIPO collects data from IP offices using a common questionnaire and methodology; because of differences in patent procedures between offices, data cannot be fully harmonized — caution when comparing across offices. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potentially pending applications (before examination vs in examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of potentially pending applications at top offices, split between (a) all patent applications awaiting a final decision (including those for which applicants have not filed a request for examination), and (b) patent applications undergoing examination for which the applicant has requested examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Application processing varies between offices (automatic vs request-for-examination models). To take account of procedural differences, pending application data are separated between the two categories. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average pendency times (first office action and final decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average pendency times (months) for first office action and for final decision at selected offices, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: EPO is the European Patent Office. WIPO collects data using a common questionnaire and methodology, but differences in patent procedures across offices make full harmonization difficult — exercise caution in cross-office comparisons. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of patent examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of patent examiners for selected offices (2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: EPO is the European Patent Office. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average years of experience of patent examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Average years of experience of patent examiners at selected offices (2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent prosecution highway is a bilateral agreement between two offices that enables applicants to request a fast-track examination whereby patent examiners can use the work already undertaken by the other office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH requests by office of first filing and office of later examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts and flows of PPH requests by office of first filing and by offices of later examination (2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: EAPO is the Eurasian Patent Organization and EPO is the European Patent Office. * indicates data based on office of earlier examination rather than office of first filing. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flows of PPH requests between offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate flows showing origin offices of first filing (e.g., US, Japan, EPO, China, Republic of Korea, Other origins) to offices of later examination (e.g., China, Republic of Korea, Japan, Canada, EPO, Other later offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Shows flows of PPH requests between offices of first filing and offices of later examination. * indicates data based on office of earlier examination rather than office of first filing. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model applications — global trend
rubrics_metrics.description: Trend in utility model applications worldwide, 2008–2022, with growth rates by year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: World totals are WIPO estimates using data covering 83 patent offices. Totals include direct national/regional filings and PCT national phase entries where applicable. China’s pre-2017 data are not comparable owing to a change in methodology; because of this break and China's large filings, accurate 2017 world growth rate is not possible. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model applications by office (top 20/offices of selected countries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility model application counts and growth rates for top 20 offices and for selected low- and middle-income country offices (2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: .. indicates not available. ARIPO is the African Regional Intellectual Property Organization. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganism deposits for patent procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Trend in microorganism deposits worldwide, 2008–2022; deposits at top international depositary authorities (2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Deposits of microorganisms for patent procedures are important for biotechnological inventions. Disclosing an invention is a requirement for receiving a patent. Lists top international depositary authorities and counts. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical table caveats — equivalent applications by origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Equivalent applications by origin data are incomplete because some offices do not report by origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) Equivalent applications by origin data are incomplete, because some offices do not report by origin. (b) The office did not report resident applications therefore the equivalent applications by origin data may be incomplete. (c) The African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI) acts as the national office for patent applications. .. indicates not available. n.a. indicates not applicable. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase entry (reporting in application tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts of PCT national phase entries by receiving office reported alongside resident/non-resident application counts in statistical tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in statistical tables of applications by office and origin. Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent grants by office and origin (and in force counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables of grants by office (resident/non-resident), equivalent grants by origin, and patents in force by office with change over previous year (2022).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes and flags in tables mirror those for applications (data completeness caveats, n.a., ..). Source: WIPO Statistics Database, August 2023.
